title: Squeezing Operator Performance Potential for the Ascend Architecture
problem: Huawei's Ascend domain-specific architecture requires manual management of memory operations and operator execution, creating complex performance bottlenecks that are difficult to diagnose with existing roofline models. Existing roofline models suffer from visualization complexity and inaccurate performance assessment when applied to Ascend's component-level architecture.
motivation: As Ascend and similar DSAs become critical AI training and inference infrastructure, the lack of effective profiling and optimization methodology prevents operators from reaching their theoretical peak performance.
method: The paper introduces a component-based roofline model that abstracts individual hardware components (compute units, memory subsystems, data pipelines) to capture per-component performance ceilings and identify bottleneck components. This model is combined with a structured optimization process derived from practical operator optimization case studies on Ascend, identifying common performance issues (e.g., memory bandwidth saturation, pipeline bubbles) and their targeted optimization strategies.
key_novelty: Component-based roofline model that abstracts Ascend hardware into distinct components to enable precise bottleneck identification and operator-level performance optimization on DSAs requiring manual memory management.
contributions: Component-based roofline model extending classical roofline analysis to Ascend's multi-component DSA architecture
Structured operator optimization methodology derived from practical case studies on Ascend
Catalog of common Ascend performance issues and their targeted optimization strategies
End-to-end optimization results showing 1.07x to 2.15x model speed improvements on real DNN workloads
limitations: Not discussed; methodology is tailored to Ascend's specific programming model and may not generalize directly to other DSAs.
primary_theme: Component-based roofline analysis and operator optimization for Ascend DSA
